step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Credimi's digital invoice processing platform. User browser traffic enters via an Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) and is routed to an EC2 Fleet running Kubernetes, which hosts domain microservices written in Scala. Upon invoice upload, the invoice microservice uploads PDF and XML files to an Amazon S3 bucket and creates an initial record entry in Amazon RDS MySQL. An S3 upload event asynchronously triggers an AWS Lambda function, which extracts invoice metadata from the XML (e.g., date, amount) and updates the corresponding record in RDS MySQL.

graph.name: Credimi Electronic Invoice Processing Architecture
graph.notes: Credimi processes electronic invoices using Kubernetes microservices on EC2, Amazon S3 for invoice document storage, AWS Lambda for async XML parsing, and Amazon RDS MySQL in Multi-AZ for metadata storage.
